history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: the temple is in the village of Goravanahalli, Koratagere taluk - CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate (Tumakuru is the district headquarters). Documented with the corrected location. Local legend: in the early 1900s a poor villager named Abbayya came into possession of a self-manifested (swayambhu) idol of Goddess Mahalakshmi; worshipping it at home, he was blessed with wealth and used it for charity, so his home came to be called Lakshmi Nivas. His brother Thotadappa also worshipped the Goddess; she appeared in his dream and asked him to build her a temple, which he did around 1900. After Thotadappa's death Chowdavya continued the poojas, but the temple was abandoned from about 1910. In 1925 the devotee Kamalamma found it in a neglected state and revived worship; she left after a year and returned in 1952 to re-establish the temple, after which it became a pilgrimage spot for Mahalakshmi devotees. A large multicoloured Raja Gopuram (with smaller arches and verandahs) fronts the sanctum; the architecture is typical South Indian style of the early 1900s.

name: Goravanahalli Maha Lakshmi Temple
town: Goravanahalli (CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate - it is the district headquarters; temple is in Koratagere taluk)
town_description: Goravanahalli is a village in Koratagere taluk of Tumakuru district (PIN 572129), set amid lush greenery close to the Theetha Reservoir built on the Suvarnamukhi River; devotees often walk around the reservoir after darshan. Well connected by road: KSRTC buses from Tumkur bus station and private buses from Kalasipalyam, Bengaluru.

travel.railway: Tumkur railway station - about 35 km (verify); Bengaluru is the other railhead.
travel.road: KSRTC buses ply daily from Tumkur bus station; private buses from Kalasipalyam, Bengaluru.
